gre_general.value: GRE General Test (valid 5 years; UTRGV code 6570) is required, unless waived for an undergraduate degree in CS or a closely related field with GPA > 3.0 or a master's degree in CS with GPA >= 3.25.
gre_general.quote: GRE General Test. GRE test scores are valid for 5 years. A waiver of the GRE requirement will be granted to applicants who show proof of completing an undergraduate degree in computer science or a closely related field with an undergraduate GPA above a 3.0 or a master...s degree in computer science with a graduate GPA of 3.25 or higher.

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for Computer Science; ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Catalog admission requirements do not state whether securing a supervisor is required before admission.

funding.value: Competitive university assistantships (GTA/GRA/GA up to 20 hrs/wk, 0.5 FTE; minimum $1,250/month or $15,000/year for GTA/GRA, $2,400/month or $28,800/year for doctoral Graduate Associate Instructors, eligible for non-resident tuition waiver) plus UTRGV Graduate Select Scholarship up to $2,000.
funding.quote: Get up to $2,000 for your graduate education with the UTRGV Graduate Select Scholarship.

also.quote: Assistantships give students the opportunity to work on campus (up to 20-hour work weeks). | Please visit with your graduate program director about the different assistantships available in your field of study. | careers.utrgv.edu for available graduate assistantship positions. | Eligible for Non-Resident Tuition Waiver: Yes | 10047 – Graduate Teaching Assistant $1,250 $15,000 $11,250 $3,750 | 10095 – Graduate Research Assistant $1,250 $15,000 $11,250 $3,750 | 10064 – Graduate Associate Instructor (doctoral level) $2,400 $28,800 $21,600 $7,200

entry_route.value: Accepts both bachelor's holders (72 credit hours) and master's holders (54 credit hours) with >= 3.0 GPA in CS, computer engineering, or a related STEM/quantitative field.
entry_route.quote: Earned bachelor's or master's degree in computer science, computer engineering, or a closely related field from a U.S. accredited institution or an international institution recognized by a credentialing service.

notes: Computer Science with Interdisciplinary Applications Ph.D. (Edinburg campus). Requires 3 letters of recommendation, letter of intent, and resume/CV. Up to 9 hours of interdisciplinary electives may include HGEN, MATH, PHYS, EECE, or MANE courses.
